annotations.title: Hebrew, Greek and New Testament links

description: Returns the curated places where a Hebrew term or idea is carried through the Greek Old Testament (the Septuagint) into the New Testament. Each entry has a title, its kind (a Greek word traced back to its Hebrew term, an idea the Greek says more openly than the Masoretic Hebrew, or a passage from a book found only in Greek), the Hebrew, Greek (Septuagint numbering) and New Testament passages, Strong's pairs for word entries, and a note saying what is and is not claimed. kind (idea, word, only), topic (lord, messiah, covenant, life) or contains narrows the list; unfiltered, every entry comes back in one large piece. Use when the user asks how a New Testament Greek word or idea traces back through the Septuagint to the Hebrew canon.

contains.description: only entries whose title or note contains this text

kind.description: idea (the Greek says it more openly), word (a Greek word traced back) or only (a book found only in Greek)

max_chars.description: optional: cap the answer at about this many characters (lists are shortened and marked truncated; use offset/nextOffset to get the rest)

name: get_septuagint_connections
